items.fcDesc: Complete loss of hold smoke and overheat detection (all nine stations lost)
items.effAc: No effect on the operational capability of the aircraft or on flight-path control; the hold detection function is a monitoring capability only and the hold carries a single blade with no suppression fitted. The aircraft continues to be controllable and dispatchable-capability is unaffected in flight; what is lost is the crew's sole means of learning of a hold smoke or overheat event, since there is no hold access and no suppression in flight.
items.effCrew: Slight increase in crew workload: the crew loses the nine-station hold indication and must rely on other cues, but takes no immediate flight-path action on loss of the detection function itself.
items.effPax: No effect on occupants; the hold is unoccupied in flight and the aircraft carries flight crew only.
items.severityRationale: Cannot ground the aircraft-level severity of a COMPLETE detection loss without the consequence of the undetected hold event it is meant to catch: the SDD states the hold has 'smoke detection at nine stations and no suppression' and the crew has no hold access in flight, so loss of detection leaves an unannunciated developing fire/overheat with no crew barrier — but the provided material does not characterise that outcome or its exposure, so the class cannot be derived. Missing: the aircraft-level effect of an undetected hold smoke/overheat event over the exposure time.

source.quote: smoke detection at nine stations along its length and no suppression

items.fcDesc: Partial loss of hold smoke and overheat detection (some detection stations lost, coverage reduced)
items.effAc: No effect on flight-path control or aircraft capability; a subset of the nine hold detection stations is lost, reducing coverage along the 108 m hold while detection remains at the surviving stations.
items.effCrew: Slight increase in crew workload: reduced detection coverage, but no immediate flight-path action arises from the partial loss itself; the crew retains indication at the remaining stations.
items.effPax: No effect on occupants; hold unoccupied in flight.
items.severityRationale: As with the complete loss, the aircraft-level severity depends on the consequence of an event occurring within the now-uncovered hold region, which the provided material does not characterise. Missing: the aircraft-level effect of a hold smoke/overheat event in the lost-coverage region.

items.fcDesc: Erroneous hold smoke or overheat warning (warning with no fire or overheat present)
items.effAc: A slight reduction in functional capabilities: a spurious hold smoke/overheat warning may prompt a precautionary land-as-soon-as-possible decision and diversion to the nearest suitable aerodrome, per the crew response the design implies for a genuine indication, with no actual fire present.
items.effCrew: Slight increase in crew workload associated with a routine diversion decision: the crew evaluates the spurious warning against other cues, but has no in-flight means to confirm hold state directly.
items.effPax: No effect on occupants; hold unoccupied in flight.
items.severityRationale: "a slight reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities, a slight increase in flightcrew workload such as routine flight plan changes" (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.2). A spurious hold warning drives a precautionary diversion with no actual hazard; the aircraft remains fully controllable and no occupant is affected.

source.quote: Land as soon as possible; the nearest suitable aerodrome, not the destination.

items.fcDesc: Undetected loss of hold smoke or overheat detection (coverage lost without crew awareness)
items.effAc: No effect on flight-path control or aircraft capability; detection coverage is lost while the crew continues normal duties believing detection is available, so no crew action is taken on the detection loss itself.
items.effCrew: The crew is unaware and takes no action; workload is unchanged until an undetected event manifests, at which point the sole monitoring barrier is absent.
items.effPax: No effect on occupants; hold unoccupied in flight.
items.severityRationale: Per AC 25.1309-1B §5.4.2 loss of annunciation is a failure condition in itself; the undetected (crew-unaware) case removes the crew's only barrier to a hold smoke/overheat event with no compensating action. The aircraft-level effect cannot be derived because the provided material does not characterise the undetected hold event outcome or its exposure. Missing: the aircraft-level consequence of an undetected hold smoke/overheat event with detection coverage silently lost.

items.fcDesc: Complete loss of ice protection
items.effAc: Loss of all ice protection means the aircraft cannot prevent or remove ice accretion on protected surfaces, inlets and probes in the icing envelope of the certification basis; unabated accretion degrades handling, performance and probe/inlet function.
items.effCrew: The crew must recognise the loss and exit or avoid icing conditions; the specific handling and performance limitation with ice protection lost is not defined in the provided material.
items.effPax: No effect on occupants beyond the aircraft effect; hold unoccupied in flight.
items.severityRationale: The SDD establishes the function ('prevents or removes ice accretion... for flight in the icing envelope of the certification basis') but does not characterise the aircraft-level consequence of a COMPLETE loss — the degradation in safety margin or handling with all protection lost while in the icing envelope. Without that consequence the class cannot be derived; abstaining rather than reaching for a level. Missing: the aircraft-level effect (safety-margin/handling reduction) of complete ice-protection loss within the certified icing envelope, and the icing-conditions limitation.

items.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.

Effects axes left empty per abstention rule.

items.fcDesc: Erroneous ice detection advisory
items.effAc: Detection advisory indicates icing when none is present; detection is advisory only and the crew may select ice protection on manually at any time, so no unwanted protection is commanded by the advisory itself. Slight reduction in functional capability at most (a performance penalty only if the crew acts on it).
items.effCrew: Slight increase in flightcrew workload to cross-check the advisory against conditions and select/deselect protection; well within crew capability.
items.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
items.severityRationale: Effects support Minor - "a slight increase in flightcrew workload" (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.2); the advisory is non-commanding and manual selection is available independently, so no significant capability reduction. Proposed for engineer confirmation.

items.effAc: One of two same-type ice detectors lost; detection is advisory and manual selection of ice protection is available at any time independent of either detector, so protection capability itself is retained. The residual icing-conditions limitation is not quantified in the provided material.

items.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.

Axes left empty per abstention rule.

Slight reduction in functional capability (bleed demand reduces pack capacity; a performance penalty is incurred).
items.effCrew: Slight increase in flightcrew workload to recognise the unwanted activation and deselect; performance penalty is applied automatically, so no manual correction is needed and none should be applied by hand.
items.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.

items.effAc: Automatic ice detection advisory is lost without annunciation; the crew is unaware and, absent the advisory, may not select ice protection when needed if it relies on the automatic advisory. The consequence in the certification icing envelope is not quantified in the provided material.

Both the icing consequence and the annunciation-loss showing are needed. Axes left empty per abstention rule.

assumptions.text: Following an asymmetric partial thrust loss at the outboard 28 m moment arm the aircraft remains controllable by the crew (does not proceed directly to hull loss), so the condition is Hazardous rather than Catastrophic.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the outboard asymmetric case sizes directional control and that continuation after loss of one engine is designed for, but provides no controllability margin data or engine-out handling to confirm the crew can arrest it.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the worst-case asymmetric thrust loss is not controllable, SF-001-PL2 rises to Catastrophic and its crew/occupant axes go to their top steps.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001-PL2 — Partial loss of thrust generation — asymmetric

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.text: An uncommanded thrust change is detected by the crew (through indication, aircraft response and alerting) and countered, keeping the condition below the top step.
assumptions.rationale: The provided material does not state the alerting or detection means for an uncommanded thrust change; the awareness assumption is needed to place SF-001-M at Major rather than higher.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an uncommanded thrust change can be undetected or uncounterable at a critical phase, SF-001-M severity increases above Major.

assumptions.text: Loss and partial loss of reverse thrust are assessed as a reduction against the 1,800 m landing requirement versus the approximately 1,080 m predicted rollout, not against a specific runway length.
assumptions.rationale: The project states braking degradation is assessed against that margin but gives no computed rollout figure for a no-reverse or degraded-reverse case, so the reduction level is inferred from the margin framing.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the margin is consumed such that the rollout exceeds 1,800 m in the loss case, SF-002-TL rises toward Hazardous; if ample margin remains it could fall to Minor.

citations.quote: Any degradation of braking is assessed against that margin and not against a runway length.

assumptions.text: The in-flight reverse deployment inhibit (weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement) and the mechanical translating-sleeve lock remain the effective barrier, so inadvertent in-flight reverse requires that barrier to be defeated.
assumptions.rationale: The document states the inhibit and lock exist but does not characterise controllability once in-flight reverse occurs, so the severity is graded against the barrier rather than a demonstrated post-deployment handling case.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the inhibit or sleeve lock does not hold, or post-deployment control is worse than assumed, SF-002-M rises toward Catastrophic.

items.fcDesc: Complete loss of payload restraint — annunciated
items.effAc: The design payload is one wind-turbine blade of up to 105 m and 72.6 t occupying the full hold length — one item, no averaging across a distributed load. Complete loss of restraint permits the 72.6 t item to shift along the 108 m hold, producing a large reduction in functional capabilities and safety margins through gross centre-of-gravity movement outside the certified envelope and structural loading of the hold hard points; the condition is not recoverable by crew action in flight — there is no in-flight adjustment of restraint and no crew access to the hold — and normally results in loss of the airplane.
items.effCrew: Fatalities or incapacitation — crew aboard, hull loss credited as not recoverable by crew action; restraint loss is annunciated but the crew has indication only and cannot re-tension in flight.
items.effPax: Multiple fatalities — hold unoccupied but crew aboard; occupant outcome is joint with the hull-loss state.
items.severityRationale: "A failure condition that would result in multiple fatalities, usually with the loss of the airplane", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.5. A single 72.6 t item shifting in a 108 m hold gives gross CG excursion and structural loading with no in-flight recovery available; top step is joint across all three axes.

items.fcDesc: Partial loss of payload restraint — loss of tension at two adjacent saddle stations
items.effAc: Loss of tension at two adjacent saddle stations is annunciated as a restraint condition requiring immediate attention — the strongest language the SDD uses about any condition. Load paths are sized so the loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours, but adjacency is the escalation the design cares about: two adjacent stations reduces the effective restraint over a length of the 72.6 t single item, reducing safety margins under manoeuvre and turbulence loads. The credited manoeuvre limitation is undefined — the design attaches no action and no manoeuvre limit, and that limit is the single largest [TBD] in the emergency procedures.
items.effCrew: Crew is annunciated and has indication only: cannot re-tension, cannot enter the hold in flight, cannot see the payload. The only available response is a flight-path limitation (minimise manoeuvre load, avoid turbulence, land as soon as possible), whose numeric limits are [TBD].
items.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
items.severityRationale: Effects grounded but severity NOT classifiable: the reduction in safety margins turns on the manoeuvre/turbulence load limitation with two adjacent stations unrestrained, which the design leaves as [TBD] (§B.10.2, open item 31) and is the single most important open value in the abnormal procedures. No class derivable without that load case.

items.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only — no injury.

The visor is a single-load-path pressure boundary and forward-fuselage structural member with no in-flight means of re-securing, so complete loss of latch/lock is credited as hull loss and the joint top step follows.

items.fcDesc: Undetected loss of payload restraint — crew unaware
items.effAc: Restraint of a single 72.6 t item along the 108 m hold is lost and the monitoring does not annunciate it; the crew continue normally and take no action. items.severityRationale: Cannot ground a class: severity turns on which stations/coverage are lost and the consequence of a hold fire/overheat in the uncovered region, which — as for SF-022-TL — rests on the un-substantiated no-suppression assumption and unquantified fire progression. Severity left empty pending that substantiation.

items.fcDesc: Erroneous hold smoke or overheat warning (warning presented with no fire or overheat present)
items.effAc: A spurious hold fire/overheat warning drives the crew to a divert-to-nearest-suitable decision and an unnecessary descent/diversion; no actual hazard exists but the aircraft is committed to a precautionary landing at a potentially unsuitable field.
items.effCrew: Significant increase in flightcrew workload to action the fire/overheat procedure, re-plan and divert, with no means to confirm the false nature of the indication (no hold access in flight).
items.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
items.severityRationale: Effects support Major: "significant increase in flightcrew workload", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3 — a spurious warning forces an unnecessary divert/precautionary landing decision the crew cannot verify, increasing workload significantly without reducing airplane capability.

source.quote: Loss of tension on any strap is annunciated in flight

items.fcDesc: Undetected loss of hold smoke or overheat detection (coverage lost with the crew unaware)
items.effAc: Detection coverage is lost without annunciation; the crew believe hold fire/overheat protection is present when it is not, so a developing hold fire or overheat in the affected region would progress with no warning and no crew recognition.
items.effCrew: The crew continue normal duties in the belief that detection is functioning and take no action; the loss is latent until an actual event that should have been annunciated is not.
items.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect from the detection loss itself.
items.severityRationale: Cannot ground a class: as an undetected (latent) loss this is the combination of loss of detection with loss of its annunciation, which under AC 25.1309-1B §5.4.2 must meet the objective of the un-annunciated effect — but that effect (undetected in-flight hold fire) is itself not established, resting on the un-substantiated no-suppression assumption. Severity left empty pending substantiation of the underlying hold-fire consequence.

source.quote: hold suppression is deliberately not fitted

items.fcDesc: Complete loss of ice protection (wing/cowl bleed protection, stabiliser electrical zones, probe/windshield heat and detection all unavailable)
items.effAc: With no ice protection available, continued flight in the icing envelope of the certification basis would permit unchecked accretion on protected surfaces, inlets and probes, reducing aerodynamic performance and the reliability of air data; the aircraft must exit and avoid icing conditions.
items.effCrew: The crew must recognise the loss and avoid or exit icing conditions; the detection advisory and the automatic performance penalty on which they normally rely are unavailable.
items.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect stated by the inputs.
items.severityRationale: Cannot ground a class: the aircraft effect depends on the icing envelope of the certification basis and the handling/performance and air-data consequence of total protection loss in that envelope, and on the crew's ability to avoid/exit icing — none of which is quantified in the provided inputs. Severity left empty rather than assumed.

source.quote: for flight in the icing envelope of the certification basis

items.fcDesc: Partial loss of ice protection
items.effAc: One or more protected zones lost while the remainder continue; bleed protection remains available from either side through the cross-bleed manifold and electrical stabiliser zones are independently supplied, but the resulting reduction in functional capability in icing depends on the icing-conditions limitation with a zone lost, which is not defined.
items.effCrew: A lost zone is annunciated; the documented crew action is to exit icing conditions if the limitation is unknown, which at present it is.
items.severityRationale: Cannot ground a severity: the icing-conditions limitation with a heated zone or bleed source lost is [TBD] (HF §B.13.2 item 2), so the reduction in safety margin the classification must derive from is not stated. Needs the icing limitation with a zone lost before a class can be committed.

source.quote: Icing-conditions limitation with a zone lost — [TBD]

items.fcDesc: Erroneous ice detection advisory
items.effAc: The advisory indicates icing when none is present, or the reverse; detection is advisory only and does not command a required protection, and manual selection of ice protection is available at any time and needs neither detector, so airplane capability is not reduced by the advisory itself.
items.effCrew: Slight increase in crew workload: the crew cross-checks conditions and selects protection manually as required; the manual selection does not depend on either detector.
items.effPax: No effect on occupants.
items.severityRationale: Effects support Minor - "slight increase in flightcrew workload", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.2. Detection is advisory, manual selection is available at any time independent of the detectors, and the performance penalty is applied automatically, so the erroneous advisory neither reduces capability nor demands action beyond the crew's routine.

source.quote: The manual selection is available at any time and does not depend on either detector

items.fcDesc: Partial loss of ice detection
items.effAc: One of two ice detectors lost while the other continues; detection is advisory and automatic activation remains available from the surviving detector, and manual selection is available at any time independent of either detector, but the effect on airplane capability when only one advisory source remains is not characterised.
items.effCrew: A detector loss is an indication; the crew can select ice protection on manually at any time, but the icing-conditions limitation with a detector lost is not defined.
items.severityRationale: Cannot ground a severity: with one of two same-type detectors lost the residual detection coverage and any icing-conditions limitation are not stated (HF §B.13.1 records only manual selection, not the limitation), so the reduction in safety margin cannot be derived. Needs the residual-detection and icing-limitation characterisation.

source.quote: Two ice detectors of the same type are installed on opposite sides

items.fcDesc: Inadvertent ice protection activation
items.effAc: Ice protection operates when not required, drawing bleed and reducing pack capacity when in use; the performance penalty of wing anti-ice in use is applied automatically to the displayed performance, so no unaccounted reduction in capability results.
items.effCrew: Slight increase in crew workload to recognise the unwanted activation and deselect; the crew does not apply the penalty by hand and should not.
items.effPax: No effect on occupants.
items.severityRationale: Effects support Minor - "slight increase in flightcrew workload", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.2. The performance penalty is applied automatically to the displayed performance and the crew may deselect at any time, so the inadvertent activation is a slight workload and bleed-management item, not a reduction in safety margin.

source.quote: performance penalty of wing anti-ice in use is applied automatically to the displayed performance

items.fcDesc: Undetected loss of ice detection
items.effAc: Ice detection is lost with no annunciation, so the crew is not prompted to select protection when icing begins; detection is advisory and manual selection remains available, but the consequence of accreting ice before the crew recognises it in the absence of the advisory is not characterised in the provided material.
items.effCrew: The crew continues normal duties with no prompt from the lost advisory; whether and how they otherwise recognise icing onset, and the icing-conditions limitation without detection, are not defined.
items.severityRationale: Cannot ground a severity: the crew-unaware case turns on how icing onset is recognised absent the advisory and on the consequence of delayed protection, neither of which is stated (detection is advisory and the icing-conditions limitation is [TBD], HF §B.13.2). Loss of the advisory undetected is also a candidate loss-of-annunciation condition. Needs the icing-onset recognition means and limitation before a class can be committed.
